definition: HVAC controls are devices and logic that regulate heating, ventilation and cooling equipment to meet specified conditions.
example: A thermostat signals the heating system when room temperature falls below its setpoint.

definition: Hypercompact stellar systems are hypothesized groups of stars that remain tightly bound to a black hole displaced from its original galactic center.
example: An astronomer looks for unusual stellar velocities to distinguish a candidate from an ordinary compact star cluster.

definition: Image and video compression encodes visual data in fewer bits by reducing redundancy, optionally discarding some detail.
example: A streaming service compresses a video so it can play over a slower connection.

definition: Imaging informatics concerns the collection, storage, exchange and use of medical images and their associated information.
example: A hospital links radiology images to the correct patient record for clinical review.

definition: Immunization is the process of acquiring protection against an infectious disease, commonly by vaccination.
example: A public health program monitors immunization coverage to identify populations lacking protection.

definition: Immunohaematology studies immune responses to blood cell antigens, especially in transfusion medicine.
example: A blood bank checks compatibility between a patient's blood and potential donor units.

definition: An in-memory database stores its working data primarily in RAM to make reads and writes fast.
example: A scoreboard uses an in-memory database to retrieve recently updated rankings.

definition: Inbound logistics manages the movement and receipt of supplies or materials into an organization.
example: A factory schedules inbound deliveries to keep ingredients available without overloading storage.

definition: Incurred but not reported describes insurance losses that have already occurred but are not yet known to the insurer.
example: An actuary estimates reserves for claims likely to arrive after the reporting date.

definition: Indentation hardness measures resistance to permanent deformation produced by pressing an indenter into a material.
example: A laboratory uses the size of an impression to compare two treated metal samples.

definition: Individual life insurance is coverage issued under an individual policy rather than obtained through a group plan.
example: A policyholder names family members as beneficiaries of their own policy.

definition: An Individualized Education Program is a written U.S. special-education plan specifying a qualifying student's goals, services and supports.
example: A school team documents a learning goal and how progress will be measured.

definition: An Individualized Family Service Plan documents U.S. early-intervention outcomes and services for an eligible infant or toddler and the family.
example: A family and service coordinator agree on support for communication during everyday routines.

definition: The Industrial Internet of Things connects industrial equipment, sensors and software to exchange data and support monitoring or control.
example: A plant tracks vibration readings from connected motors to schedule maintenance.

definition: Industrial statistics applies statistical methods to manufacturing, process improvement and other industrial decisions.
example: A quality engineer uses a control chart to distinguish routine variation from an unusual change.

definition: Infant development concerns physical, cognitive, communicative and social changes during infancy.
example: A researcher observes changes in how infants respond to familiar voices.

definition: Ingredient functionality concerns how an ingredient contributes to a food's properties or processing behavior.
example: A formulation team uses a starch's thickening properties to improve sauce consistency.

definition: Integrative biology combines evidence or methods across biological disciplines and scales to explain living systems.
example: A team combines biomechanics and ecology to explain how animals move across different habitats.

definition: Intellectual property concerns legal rights in certain creations, inventions, identifying marks and protected information.
example: A publishing team checks which rights it needs to reproduce an illustration.

definition: Intended Nationally Determined Contributions were climate commitments proposed by countries before or in connection with joining the Paris Agreement.
example: A policy analyst compares a country's initial intended contribution with its later formally submitted contribution.

definition: The ISS Environmental Control and Life Support System maintains conditions needed for crew survival aboard the International Space Station.
example: The system manages cabin air quality and recovers reusable water.

definition: IT governance assigns decision rights and accountability for directing and overseeing an organization's information technology.
example: A board defines who can approve major technology investments and how results will be monitored.

definition: Itô's lemma gives the differential of a function of an Itô process, accounting for the second-order contribution of stochastic variation.
example: An analyst derives the dynamics of the logarithm of a modeled asset price.

definition: A knowledge graph organizes entities, attributes and relationships into a graph with explicit meanings for its connections.
example: A museum links artists to their works so researchers can trace shared exhibitions.

definition: Labor market trends are changes over time in indicators such as employment, wages, vacancies or participation.
example: A workforce planner compares several years of vacancy rates across occupations.

definition: Labour economics studies how workers and employers interact and how wages, employment and working conditions are determined.
example: An economist models how access to training affects wages and job mobility.

definition: Labour law concerns legal rules governing employment relationships, working conditions and collective worker rights.
example: A legal team reviews how a collective bargaining provision applies to a shift change.

definition: Land-atmosphere interactions are exchanges of energy, water and other materials between the land surface and the air above it.
example: A climate model uses soil moisture to estimate how much surface energy goes into evaporation.

definition: Large language models are large machine-learning models trained to learn patterns in language and perform tasks such as generating or transforming text.
example: An assistant turns a long project update into a short summary for review.

definition: Laser engineering applies optical and engineering principles to the design and integration of lasers and laser-based systems.
example: An engineer matches a laser's wavelength and beam properties to an optical measurement task.

definition: Laser printing uses a laser to form an electrostatic image on a photosensitive surface so toner can be transferred and fused to paper.
example: An office printer produces sharp text by depositing toner only where the page image requires it.

definition: Latin American and Latino studies examines histories, cultures and societies of Latin America and Latino communities, often including cross-border connections.
example: A course compares migration narratives in Latin American and U.S. Latino literature.

definition: Law enforcement operations concerns how agencies coordinate personnel, procedures and resources to carry out public-safety duties.
example: An agency coordinates call dispatch and traffic diversion during a road closure.

definition: Law enforcement practices are the methods and professional procedures used to carry out, document and review law enforcement work.
example: A supervisor reviews whether officers documented incident decisions consistently.

definition: Lawful interception is the legally authorized collection of specified communications or related data, subject to defined procedures and oversight.
example: A compliance team reviews whether an authorization covers the requested records.

definition: Leisure education helps people develop the knowledge and skills to choose and participate in personally meaningful leisure activities.
example: A community program teaches participants how to identify accessible recreational options.

definition: Letterforms are the designed visual shapes of written letters.
example: A type designer adjusts the curve of a lowercase a to improve readability.

definition: Librarianship is the profession of organizing information resources and helping people find, evaluate and use them.
example: A librarian catalogs a collection and teaches patrons to search it efficiently.

definition: Linguistic morphology studies how meaningful units combine within words and how word forms express grammatical distinctions.
example: A linguist analyzes how a plural suffix changes a noun's number.

definition: Loan agreements are contracts that define the amount borrowed, repayment terms and obligations of the borrower and lender.
example: A business reviews a loan agreement to identify its repayment schedule and collateral obligations.
